subject: AtlasAI — replacement economics and staged pilot ask
messages:
From: Ben Shaw <ben.shaw@atlasai.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: AtlasAI Procurement <procurement@atlasai.com>
Date: 2026-10-28T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluating replacement options (SwitchCloud -> Redwood)

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers looked promising. Procurement asked me to get a concrete economics comparison vs our incumbent (SwitchCloud). They want a clear side-by-side we can show leadership: 12-month run-rate, pilot discount, and incremental ops cost to migrate (eg. egress + integration).

Two asks to make the case internally:
- Can you produce a 12-month TCO with tiered discount scenarios (0%, 15%, 25%) and a recommended pilot concession?
- Can you confirm which runtime features (prefix/KV caching, batching windows, quantization) change the unit cost materially for our workloads? We run 90% chat workload at p95 length ~600 tokens.

If helpful, I can share a sanitized usage export. Prefer a quick call next week to review the worksheet.

Cheers,
Ben

--
Ben Shaw
Head of Platform Engineering, AtlasAI
ben.shaw@atlasai.com

Date: 2026-10-29T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluating replacement options (SwitchCloud -> Redwood)

Hi Ben — thanks for the clear asks. Attaching a first-pass TCO and a small run-rate calculator (both stubs below) that model the three discount bands you mentioned. Quick notes upfront:

- Base assumptions: your export (sanitized) + our pilot profile (30k monthly active users, p95 length 600, 90% chat).
- Cost levers that move the needle: intelligent KV/prefix caching (can reduce token cost by 18–35% depending on hit-rate), batching policy (throughput-sensitive vs latency-sensitive windows), and quantization profile on the model variant.
- Pilot recommendation: 8-week canary with 50% traffic routed to Redwood + a one-time migration credit to cover egress and implementation (~$25k in our model) — this keeps commitment low while proving production metrics.

Attachments: atlas_tco_v1.xlsx (xlsx) — TCO w/ tier scenarios; runcalc_v1.xlsx (xlsx) — usage-to-cost calculator.

If you want, Connor can run the KV hit-rate sensitivity with your actual prefix distribution; he’s cc’d. Would you be available for a 45-minute review Thurs 11/4?

Best,
Irene
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Shaw <ben.shaw@atlasai.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: AtlasAI Procurement <procurement@atlasai.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluating replacement options (SwitchCloud -> Redwood)

Irene — the deck looks good, thanks. A few follow-ups from procurement after our internal sync:

1) They want to see an explicit "price-match" path: if SwitchCloud offers a lower list rate post-negotiation, what components would Redwood match (unit price vs credits vs SLA)?
2) On the migration credit: procurement prefers a structured rebate tied to go-live (eg. 50% upfront credit, 50% after month-2 if SLOs met). Can Redwood do that?
3) Ops question: SwitchCloud claims they have a proprietary batching optimization that reduces their token cost by ~12% at scale. Can your runtime replicate this for our workload, or would that be part of a custom engineering scope?

Also, attached a snapshot SwitchCloud provided of their runtime config — can your team quickly confirm the biggest compatibility gaps?

Ben
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-14T15:43:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Evaluating replacement options (SwitchCloud -> Redwood)

Team — forwarding AtlasAI thread and procurement asks. Key negotiation points and my proposed play:

Quoted message below for context.

Proposed commercial posture:
- Price-match policy: match unit token price for the first 6 months if AtlasAI provides SwitchCloud's redlineed agreement; otherwise offer an equivalent economic package via blended credits to preserve our published SLAs. Avoid permanently dropping published list.
- Migration credit structure: agree to staged rebate (50% on signature, 50% tied to month-2 SLOs). Include clear acceptance tests (p95 latency parity, KV hit-rate delta <10%).
- Pilot guardrails: 8-week canary, 50% traffic, no long-term commit until post-pilot review. Offer a one-time dev/onboard credit to cover egress.

Technical notes (Connor):
- KV/prefix caching: high potential — if AtlasAI can deliver a prefix histogram we can model hit-rate. With a 40% hit-rate our calc shows ~22% cost reduction vs naive serving.
- Batching: we can mirror SwitchCloud's batching windows with our runtime flags; any proprietary optimizations they claim are likely kernel-level heuristics — we can approximate with config but would treat any deep engineering parity as a time-and-materials scope if it requires custom kernel work.

Risks and ask for leadership sign-off:
- Matching too aggressively on list price sets a precedent; prefer matching economics via term-limited credits where possible.
- Legal/finance: need approval for 6-month price-match and template language on acceptance criteria.

Action items:
- Marissa: draft a short "price-match vs credit" commercial language (two options) for legal review.
- Jordan: prepare a p&l showing impact of a 6-month match at 15%/25% bands (fast sim).
- Connor: ask AtlasAI for a prefix histogram + attach switchcloud_config_snapshot.txt and run the KV hit-rate sensitivity; give a conservative estimate within 3 business days.

I'm looping Legal if we get a hard ask from procurement. Thoughts?

Thanks,
Irene
